passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Command the Israelites to send away from the camp anyone with a skin disease, anyone who has a bodily discharge, and anyone who is defiled by a dead body.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to command the Israelites.
The Israelites must send certain people away from the camp.
They must send away anyone with a skin disease.
They must send away anyone with a bodily discharge.
They must send away anyone who is defiled by a dead body.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ צַ֚ו אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וִֽישַׁלְּחוּ֙ מִן־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה כָּל־ צָר֖וּעַ וְכָל־ זָ֑ב וְכֹ֖ל טָמֵ֥א לָנָֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: You must send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses a command for the Israelites.
God told the Israelites to send away certain people from the camp.
They must send away both males and females.
They must send them outside the camp.
God lives among the Israelites.
God does not want the camp to become unclean.
Sending these people away keeps the camp clean.
passages.original: מִזָּכָ֤ר עַד־ נְקֵבָה֙ תְּשַׁלֵּ֔חוּ אֶל־ מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה תְּשַׁלְּח֑וּם וְלֹ֤א יְטַמְּאוּ֙ אֶת־ מַ֣חֲנֵיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י שֹׁכֵ֥ן בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: So the Israelites did this, sending such people outside the camp. They did just as the LORD had instructed Moses.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites obeyed the LORD.
The LORD had spoken to Moses.
The LORD told Moses to send certain people outside the camp.
The Israelites sent those people outside the camp.
The Israelites did exactly as the LORD commanded Moses.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־ כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְשַׁלְּח֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם אֶל־ מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites that when a man or woman acts unfaithfully against the LORD by committing any sin against another, that person is guilty and must confess the sin he has committed. He must make full restitution, add a fifth to its value, and give all this to the one he has wronged.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
A man or a woman may sin against another person.
This sin is also unfaithfulness against the LORD.
That person becomes guilty.
The guilty person must confess the sin he or she has done.
The guilty person must make full restitution for the wrong.
The guilty person must add one fifth to the value of what was taken or lost.
The guilty person must give all this to the one he or she has wronged.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּר֮ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־ אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּ֤י יַעֲשׂוּ֙ מִכָּל־ חַטֹּ֣את הָֽאָדָ֔ם לִמְעֹ֥ל מַ֖עַל בַּיהוָ֑ה וְאָֽשְׁמָ֖ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִֽוא׃ וְהִתְוַדּ֗וּ אֶֽת־ חַטָּאתָם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂוּ֒ וְהֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־ אֲשָׁמוֹ֙ בְּרֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַחֲמִישִׁת֖וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑יו וְנָתַ֕ן לַאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָשַׁ֥ם לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But if the man has no relative to whom restitution can be made for the wrong, the restitution belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest along with the ram of atonement, by which the atonement is made for him.
passages.sermon:
A man may do wrong to another person.
Sometimes, the wronged person has no living relative.
No one can receive restitution for the wrong.
In this case, the guilty man must still make restitution.
He must give the restitution to the LORD.
He must give it to the priest.
He must also bring a ram for atonement.
The priest will use the ram to make atonement for the guilty man.
passages.original: וְאִם־ אֵ֨ין לָאִ֜ישׁ גֹּאֵ֗ל לְהָשִׁ֤יב הָאָשָׁם֙ אֵלָ֔יו הָאָשָׁ֛ם הַמּוּשָׁ֥ב לַיהוָ֖ה לַכֹּהֵ֑ן מִלְּבַ֗ד אֵ֚יל הַכִּפֻּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְכַפֶּר־ בּ֖וֹ עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Every sacred contribution the Israelites bring to the priest shall belong to him.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites are God's chosen people.
The Israelites bring sacred contributions.
These contributions are holy gifts.
The Israelites give these gifts to the priest.
The priest receives these gifts.
The gifts belong to the priest.
passages.original: וְכָל־ תְּרוּמָ֞ה לְכָל־ קָדְשֵׁ֧י בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ יַקְרִ֥יבוּ לַכֹּהֵ֖ן ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Each man’s sacred gifts are his own, but whatever he gives to the priest will belong to the priest.”
passages.sermon: Each man owns his own sacred gifts.\r\nIf a man gives something to the priest, it will belong to the priest.
passages.original: וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־ קֳדָשָׁ֖יו ל֣וֹ יִהְי֑וּ אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ יִתֵּ֥ן לַכֹּהֵ֖ן ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that if any man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him by sleeping with another man, and it is concealed from her husband and her impurity is undetected (since there is no witness against her and she was not caught in the act), and if a feeling of jealousy comes over her husband and he suspects his wife who has defiled herself—or if a feeling of jealousy comes over him and he suspects her even though she has not defiled herself— then he is to bring his wife to the priest. He must also bring for her an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He is not to pour oil over it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, an offering of memorial as a reminder of iniquity.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
Moses must say this to them.
If a man’s wife goes astray, she is unfaithful to him.
She sleeps with another man.
Her husband does not know.
No one saw her.
She was not caught.
There is no witness against her.
She has become impure.
A spirit of jealousy comes over her husband.
He suspects his wife.
She may have become impure.
Or, a spirit of jealousy comes over him.
He suspects his wife, but she has not become impure.
The man must bring his wife to the priest.
He must also bring an offering for her.
The offering is a tenth of an ephah of barley flour.
He must not pour oil on it.
He must not put frankincense on it.
This is a grain offering for jealousy.
It is a memorial offering.
It reminds people of iniquity.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ כִּֽי־ תִשְׂטֶ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וּמָעֲלָ֥ה ב֖וֹ מָֽעַל׃ וְשָׁכַ֨ב אִ֣ישׁ אֹתָהּ֮ שִׁכְבַת־ זֶרַע֒ וְנֶעְלַם֙ מֵעֵינֵ֣י אִישָׁ֔הּ וְנִסְתְּרָ֖ה וְהִ֣יא נִטְמָ֑אָה וְעֵד֙ אֵ֣ין בָּ֔הּ וְהִ֖וא לֹ֥א נִתְפָּֽשָׂה׃ וְעָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧יו רֽוּחַ־ קִנְאָ֛ה וְקִנֵּ֥א אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְהִ֣וא נִטְמָ֑אָה אוֹ־ עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤יו רֽוּחַ־ קִנְאָה֙ וְקִנֵּ֣א אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וְהִ֖יא לֹ֥א נִטְמָֽאָה׃ וְהֵבִ֨יא הָאִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ אִשְׁתּוֹ֮ אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְהֵבִ֤יא אֶת־ קָרְבָּנָהּ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ עֲשִׂירִ֥ת הָאֵיפָ֖ה קֶ֣מַח שְׂעֹרִ֑ים לֹֽא־ יִצֹ֨ק עָלָ֜יו שֶׁ֗מֶן וְלֹֽא־ יִתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ לְבֹנָ֔ה כִּֽי־ מִנְחַ֤ת קְנָאֹת֙ ה֔וּא מִנְחַ֥ת זִכָּר֖וֹן מַזְכֶּ֥רֶת עָוֺֽן׃

passages.text: The priest is to bring the wife forward and have her stand before the LORD.
passages.sermon: The priest takes the wife.\r\nThe priest brings her forward.\r\nThe priest makes her stand before the LORD.
passages.original: וְהִקְרִ֥יב אֹתָ֖הּ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְהֶֽעֱמִדָ֖הּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then he is to take some holy water in a clay jar and put some of the dust from the tabernacle floor into the water.
passages.sermon:
The priest takes holy water.
He puts the holy water in a clay jar.
The priest takes dust from the floor of the tabernacle.
He puts the dust into the water.
passages.original: וְלָקַ֧ח הַכֹּהֵ֛ן מַ֥יִם קְדֹשִׁ֖ים בִּכְלִי־ חָ֑רֶשׂ וּמִן־ הֶֽעָפָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִהְיֶה֙ בְּקַרְקַ֣ע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן יִקַּ֥ח הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְנָתַ֥ן אֶל־ הַמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: After the priest has the woman stand before the LORD, he is to let down her hair and place in her hands the grain offering of memorial, which is the grain offering for jealousy. The priest is to hold the bitter water that brings a curse.
passages.sermon:
The priest brings the woman before the LORD.
The priest lets down the woman's hair.
The priest puts the grain offering of memorial in the woman's hands.
This grain offering is for jealousy.
The priest holds the bitter water that brings a curse.
passages.original: וְהֶעֱמִ֨יד הַכֹּהֵ֥ן אֶֽת־ הָאִשָּׁה֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֒ וּפָרַע֙ אֶת־ רֹ֣אשׁ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְנָתַ֣ן עַל־ כַּפֶּ֗יהָ אֵ֚ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַזִּכָּר֔וֹן מִנְחַ֥ת קְנָאֹ֖ת הִ֑וא וּבְיַ֤ד הַכֹּהֵן֙ יִהְי֔וּ מֵ֥י הַמָּרִ֖ים הַמְאָֽרֲרִֽים׃

passages.text: And he is to put the woman under oath and say to her, ‘If no other man has slept with you and you have not gone astray and become defiled while under your husband’s authority, may you be immune to this bitter water that brings a curse.
passages.sermon:
The priest stands before the woman.
The priest puts the woman under oath.
The priest speaks to the woman.
He says, "If no other man has slept with you,
and if you have not gone astray from your husband,
and if you have not become defiled while under your husband's authority,
then you will be free from this bitter water that brings a curse."
The bitter water is the water that brings a curse.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ אֹתָ֜הּ הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאָמַ֤ר אֶל־ הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אִם־ לֹ֨א שָׁכַ֥ב אִישׁ֙ אֹתָ֔ךְ וְאִם־ לֹ֥א שָׂטִ֛ית טֻמְאָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת אִישֵׁ֑ךְ הִנָּקִ֕י מִמֵּ֛י הַמָּרִ֥ים הַֽמְאָרֲרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: But if you have gone astray while under your husband’s authority and have defiled yourself and lain carnally with a man other than your husband’— and the priest shall have the woman swear under the oath of the curse—‘then may the LORD make you an attested curse among your people by making your thigh shrivel and your belly swell.
passages.sermon:
The priest stands before the woman.
The priest speaks to the woman.
The priest addresses a woman suspected of adultery.
The woman is married.
The woman is under her husband's authority.
If you have gone astray from your husband,
If you have defiled yourself,
If another man has slept with you,
If this happened while your husband was still alive,
The priest makes the woman swear an oath.
The priest gives her the oath of the curse.
The priest says to the woman,
“May the LORD make you a curse among your people.
May the LORD make you an example by this curse.
May the LORD cause your thigh to shrivel.
May the LORD cause your belly to swell.”
passages.original: וְאַ֗תְּ כִּ֥י שָׂטִ֛ית תַּ֥חַת אִישֵׁ֖ךְ וְכִ֣י נִטְמֵ֑את וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אִ֥ישׁ בָּךְ֙ אֶת־ שְׁכָבְתּ֔וֹ מִֽבַּלְעֲדֵ֖י אִישֵֽׁךְ׃ וְהִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ הַכֹּהֵ֥ן אֶֽת־ הָֽאִשָּׁה֮ בִּשְׁבֻעַ֣ת הָאָלָה֒ וְאָמַ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ לָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה אוֹתָ֛ךְ לְאָלָ֥ה וְלִשְׁבֻעָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ עַמֵּ֑ךְ בְּתֵ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־ יְרֵכֵךְ֙ נֹפֶ֔לֶת וְאֶת־ בִּטְנֵ֖ךְ צָבָֽה׃

passages.text: May this water that brings a curse enter your stomach and cause your belly to swell and your thigh to shrivel.’ Then the woman is to say, ‘Amen, Amen.’
passages.sermon:
The priest speaks to the woman.
He says, "This water brings a curse."
He says, "May this water enter your stomach."
He says, "May it cause your belly to swell."
He says, "May it cause your thigh to shrivel."
The woman must answer.
She must say, "Amen, Amen."
passages.original: וּ֠בָאוּ הַמַּ֨יִם הַמְאָרְרִ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ בְּֽמֵעַ֔יִךְ לַצְבּ֥וֹת בֶּ֖טֶן וְלַנְפִּ֣ל יָרֵ֑ךְ וְאָמְרָ֥ה הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אָמֵ֥ן׀ אָמֵֽן׃

passages.text: And the priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
passages.sermon: The priest is a leader in Israel.\r\nThe priest writes the curses on a scroll.\r\nThe priest washes the curses off the scroll into the bitter water.
passages.original: וְ֠כָתַב אֶת־ הָאָלֹ֥ת הָאֵ֛לֶּה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בַּסֵּ֑פֶר וּמָחָ֖ה אֶל־ מֵ֥י הַמָּרִֽים׃

passages.text: He is to have the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and it will enter her and cause her bitter suffering.
passages.sermon:
The priest gives the woman the bitter water that brings a curse.
The woman drinks the bitter water.
The bitter water enters her body.
The bitter water causes her to suffer.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁקָה֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אֶת־ מֵ֥י הַמָּרִ֖ים הַמְאָֽרֲרִ֑ים וּבָ֥אוּ בָ֛הּ הַמַּ֥יִם הַֽמְאָרֲרִ֖ים לְמָרִֽים׃

passages.text: The priest shall take from her hand the grain offering for jealousy, wave it before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
passages.sermon:
The priest stands before the woman.
The woman holds the grain offering for jealousy in her hand.
The priest takes the grain offering from her hand.
The priest waves the grain offering before the LORD.
The priest brings the grain offering to the altar.
passages.original: וְלָקַ֤ח הַכֹּהֵן֙ מִיַּ֣ד הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֵ֖ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַקְּנָאֹ֑ת וְהֵנִ֤יף אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְהִקְרִ֥יב אֹתָ֖הּ אֶל־ הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Then the priest is to take a handful of the grain offering as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar; after that he is to have the woman drink the water.
passages.sermon:
The priest takes a handful of the grain offering.
This handful is called the memorial portion.
The priest burns the memorial portion on the altar.
After burning the offering, the priest gives the woman the water to drink.
passages.original: וְקָמַ֨ץ הַכֹּהֵ֤ן מִן־ הַמִּנְחָה֙ אֶת־ אַזְכָּ֣רָתָ֔הּ וְהִקְטִ֖יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה וְאַחַ֛ר יַשְׁקֶ֥ה אֶת־ הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אֶת־ הַמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: When he has made her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, then the water that brings a curse will enter her and cause bitter suffering; her belly will swell, her thigh will shrivel, and she will become accursed among her people.
passages.sermon:
The priest gives the woman the water to drink.
If the woman has defiled herself, she has been unfaithful to her husband.
The water brings a curse.
The water enters her and causes bitter suffering.
Her belly swells.
Her thigh shrivels.
The woman becomes accursed among her people.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁקָ֣הּ אֶת־ הַמַּ֗יִם וְהָיְתָ֣ה אִֽם־ נִטְמְאָה֮ וַתִּמְעֹ֣ל מַ֣עַל בְּאִישָׁהּ֒ וּבָ֨אוּ בָ֜הּ הַמַּ֤יִם הַמְאָֽרֲרִים֙ לְמָרִ֔ים וְצָבְתָ֣ה בִטְנָ֔הּ וְנָפְלָ֖ה יְרֵכָ֑הּ וְהָיְתָ֧ה הָאִשָּׁ֛ה לְאָלָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב עַמָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be unaffected and able to conceive children.
passages.sermon:
The woman stands accused of unfaithfulness.
If the woman has not defiled herself, she is innocent.
If the woman is clean, she will not be harmed.
She will be able to conceive children.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֤א נִטְמְאָה֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּטְהֹרָ֖ה הִ֑וא וְנִקְּתָ֖ה וְנִזְרְעָ֥ה זָֽרַע׃

passages.text: This is the law of jealousy when a wife goes astray and defiles herself while under her husband’s authority, or when a feeling of jealousy comes over a husband and he suspects his wife. He is to have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest is to apply to her this entire law.
passages.sermon:
This is the law of jealousy.
A wife may go astray while she is under her husband’s authority.
She may defile herself.
A husband may feel jealous.
He may suspect his wife.
The husband must bring the woman before the LORD.
The priest must apply this entire law to her.
passages.original: זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַקְּנָאֹ֑ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּשְׂטֶ֥ה אִשָּׁ֛ה תַּ֥חַת אִישָׁ֖הּ וְנִטְמָֽאָה׃ א֣וֹ אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תַּעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֛יו ר֥וּחַ קִנְאָ֖ה וְקִנֵּ֣א אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְהֶעֱמִ֤יד אֶת־ הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְעָ֤שָׂה לָהּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַתּוֹרָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: The husband will be free from guilt, but the woman shall bear her iniquity.”
passages.sermon: The husband will not be guilty.\r\nThe woman will carry her own guilt.
passages.original: וְנִקָּ֥ה הָאִ֖ישׁ מֵעָוֺ֑ן וְהָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַהִ֔וא תִּשָּׂ֖א אֶת־ עֲוֺנָֽהּ׃פ
